key_insight: In disordered perovskite nanocrystal solids, exciton transport is governed more by energetic disorder than by structural polydispersity.
engineering_relevance: Ligand length is a practical design lever for tuning nanocrystal ordering and energy transport in perovskite optoelectronic devices such as LEDs, lasers, and solar cells.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared disorder effects across nanocrystal solids synthesized with different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked transport efficiency to structural vs energetic disorder
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that longer alkyl-chain ligands produce more monodisperse nanocrystals but stronger quantum confinement and increased energetic disorder, and these samples show less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: Improving size uniformity alone may not improve performance if ligand-induced energetic disorder remains high.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
